article_title: Identifying Entrustable Professional Activities for Shared Decision Making in Postgraduate Medical Education: A National Delphi Study.
citation: Baghus A, Giroldi E, Muris J, Stiggelbout A, van de Pol M, Timmerman A, van der Weijden T. (2020). Identifying Entrustable Professional Activities for Shared Decision Making in Postgraduate Medical Education: A National Delphi Study. Academic Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/ACM.0000000000003618
title: Four entrustable professional activities for shared decision making in postgraduate medical education
description: The article's final list comprises 4 SDM EPAs: (1) the resident discusses the desirability of SDM with the patient, (2) the resident discusses the options for management with the patient, (3) the resident explores the patient's preferences and deliberations, and (4) the resident takes a well-argued decision together with the patient. Each EPA carries associated behavioral indicators that "support tailored learning processes by providing room to address the building blocks of the EPAs, depending on individual learning needs during workplace learning." The EPAs describe SDM behaviors formulated for the end-stage proficiency level of postgraduate training and integrate competency domains such as medical knowledge, communication, collaboration, and EBM.
requirements: Used to support focused observation and feedback during workplace learning, and to guide assessment of the resident's level of competence, with individual learning processes as a starting point to prevent box-checking use
constraints: Developed and validated at the national level in the Netherlands because SDM is sensitive to language and culture; the EPAs include generic elements other countries can adapt
examples: The EPAs were derived from a literature review of SDM frameworks and 17 expert interviews, then refined through 3 Delphi rounds in which overlapping or too-directive EPAs were merged or reformulated.

article_title: Differentiated need support by teachers: Student-specific provision of autonomy and structure and relations with student motivation.
citation: Domen, J., Hornstra, L., Weijers, D., van der Veen, I., & Peetsma, T. (2020). Differentiated need support by teachers: Student‐specific provision of autonomy and structure and relations with student motivation. British Journal of Educational Psychology, 90(2), 403–423. https://doi.org/10.1111/bjep.12302
title: Self‐determination theory: need‐supportive teaching through autonomy support and structure as two independent dimensions
description: The article organises its inquiry with self‐determination theory, in which "teachers can support their students' engagement in learning by supporting their psychological needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness". Autonomy support is teaching that fosters students' autonomous functioning, for example by providing choice, while structure is the amount and clarity of information helping students know what is expected and how to achieve it. Crucially, "autonomy support and structure are described in SDT as two independent dimensions" rather than opposite ends of one continuum, and providing both is considered most conducive to motivation.
requirements: Teachers who provide both autonomy support and structure, since providing both is described as most conducive to student motivation
constraints: The article notes prior research suggests many teachers find it difficult to provide structure in an autonomy‐supportive way
target_learning_goals: Fostering autonomous motivation and engagement in learning
examples: The study operationalised the two dimensions with adapted teacher and student versions of the Teachers as Social Context Questionnaire and tested their relations with motivation in multilevel mediation models

article_title: Gamification in Physical Education: Evaluation of Impact on Motivation and Academic Performance within Higher Education.
citation: Ferriz-Valero Alberto; Østerlie Ove; García Martínez Salvador; García-Jaén Miguel. (2020). Gamification in Physical Education: Evaluation of Impact on Motivation and Academic Performance within Higher Education. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph17124465
title: Self-determination theory continuum of motivation as framework for evaluating gamification in PE
description: The study uses self-determination theory (SDT) as "a macro-theory to understand the role of motivation within the educational environment", ordering intrinsic motivation, extrinsic motivation and amotivation on a self-determination continuum from highest to lowest. Within extrinsic motivation it distinguishes external regulation (behaviours governed by external rewards or punishments), introjected regulation (avoiding guilt or seeking recognition) and identified regulation (voluntary activity deemed beneficial). The CMEF questionnaire measured these five factors to test whether gamification shifted students along the continuum.
requirements: A validated instrument distinguishing the five motivational regulations (CMEF, 20 items, Likert 1–5, α > 0.70)
constraints: The study did not measure integrated regulation, which the authors name as a limitation for future studies with university students
target_learners: university students in physical education teacher education
target_learning_goals: understanding motivational regulation of learning in physical education
examples: External regulation items were framed as e.g. 'because it is seen as good by the teacher', capturing reward-contingent behaviour regulated by the game's point system

article_title: Predicting Bullying through Motivation and Teaching Styles in Physical Education.
citation: Montero-Carretero C., Barbado D., Cervelló E. (2020). Predicting Bullying through Motivation and Teaching Styles in Physical Education. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph17010087
title: Self-determination theory model of bullying in physical education
description: The article tests a self-determination theory (SDT) predictor model in which the PE teacher's supportive style predicts students' satisfaction of basic psychological needs (autonomy, competence, relatedness), which predicts self-determined motivation, which in turn predicts bullying perpetration and victimization. The authors state the results "are in line with the SDT postulates" and underline teachers' potential responsibility in reducing bullying by supporting autonomy and avoiding a controlling style.
requirements: Measurement of teacher supportive style, BPN satisfaction, self-determined motivation, and bullying via validated questionnaires (EPES-PE, BPN scale, CMPE, EBIP-Q)
constraints: Cross-sectional, correlational, single sample; the authors state this "does not allow for the establishment of causal relationships"
target_learners: Primary and secondary school students aged 11–15 in physical education classes
target_learning_goals: Reduce bullying perpetration and victimization; support motivation and basic psychological need satisfaction in PE

article_title: Does group cohesion foster self-directed learning for medical students? A longitudinal study.
citation: Kim S, Yang Eunbae B. (2020). Does group cohesion foster self-directed learning for medical students? A longitudinal study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1962-7
title: Korean self-directed learning readiness scale (SDLRS) and group cohesiveness scale (GCS) instruments
description: The study used two Likert-type instruments administered annually. The SDLRS was a Korean revision for college students with "a total of 23 items" across seven constructs including love of learning, openness towards learning, and self-perception, on a five-point scale. The GCS is "a seven-item, five-point, Likert-type scale" originally designed for psychiatric inpatients but suggested for any group activity involving interaction; it was translated into Korean and back-translated for this study, with Cronbach's alphas of .770 to .920 across years.
requirements: Permission from the instrument author was obtained for SDLRS use; GCS required translation and back-translation with researcher consensus
constraints: Few translated Korean versions of SDL instruments exist, and GCS was originally designed for psychiatric inpatients

citation: Kim S, Yang Eunbae B. (2020). Does group cohesion foster self-directed learning for medical students? A longitudinal study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-020-1962-7
title: Self-directed learning as a socially embedded concept involving interaction with peers and context
description: The article frames SDL not as a purely individual activity but as a dynamic concept with functional relationships to metacognitive behavior, the social context of learning, and pedagogical interaction. Citing Giddings, it notes "SDL is not just an individual's work," and reports that workplace factors such as trust, mutual respect, and collaboration enhance SDL. The study's finding that group cohesion predicts SDLRS variance supports this account, consistent with an earlier study the authors cite that SDL "is a concept that involves interactions or coherence with colleagues to exchange information."
requirements: A learning environment with opportunities for peer interaction, since SDL involves exchanging information with peers and teachers
constraints: Learning behaviors such as SDL may vary widely in a new and unfamiliar context, so the importance of context must be stressed

article_title: Institutional strategies related to test-taking behavior in low stakes assessment.
citation: Schüttpelz-Brauns, K., Hecht, M., Hardt, K., Karay, Y., Zupanic, M., & Kämmer, J. E. (2020). Institutional strategies related to test-taking behavior in low stakes assessment. Advances in Health Sciences Education, 25(2), 321–335. https://doi.org/10.1007/s10459-019-09928-y
title: Self-determination theory as a framework for classifying institutional strategies affecting test-taking effort
description: The article uses Ryan and Deci's self-determination theory to classify institutional strategies for increasing serious test-taking behavior. Motivation is conceived as a continuum from amotivation through extrinsic motivation (external regulation, introjection, identification) to intrinsic motivation, which occurs when autonomy, competence, and relatedness needs are satisfied. The authors chose for analysis only strategies assignable to SDT, noting it "is a general motivation theory which holds true for different aspects of motivation in an individual's life, including education and learning". Each studied strategy is mapped to an SDT level: consequences and assessment presentation to external regulation, individuality of discussed results and mentor discussion to introjection or relatedness, and choice to autonomy.
requirements: Strategies must be classifiable into an SDT motivational level for the framework to generate predictions about their effects
constraints: The authors found that not all strategies belonging to a motivational theory are related to serious test-taking behavior in all conditions, and students may be on different motivational levels, so strategies can have differentiated effects
target_learning_goals: motivation quality and test-taking effort in low-stakes assessment
examples: The article maps consequences for not participating and assessment presentation to external regulation, mentor discussion to relatedness or introjection, and choice to autonomy support

article_title: Influence of Emotional Intelligence, Motivation and Resilience on Academic Performance and the Adoption of Healthy Lifestyle Habits among Adolescents.
citation: Trigueros Rubén, Aguilar-Parra José M., Cangas Adolfo J., Bermejo Rosario, Ferrandiz Carmen, López-Liria Remedios. (2019). Influence of Emotional Intelligence, Motivation and Resilience on Academic Performance and the Adoption of Healthy Lifestyle Habits among Adolescents. International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health. https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph16162810
title: SDT-based structural model linking emotions, resilience and motivation to academic and health outcomes in PE
description: The article develops a structural equations model applying principles of Self-Determination Theory, which distinguishes amotivation, controlled motivation and self-motivation, with self-motivation defined as when "individuals persist and adhere to a series of behaviors without the need for external stimuli". The model chains emotional intelligence to emotional state, emotions to resilience and self-motivation, and self-motivation to academic performance and physical activity intention. It was tested with 615 secondary students and showed adequate fit (CFI = 0.95, RMSEA = 0.062).
requirements: Each latent variable in the model had at least two indicators, per the article's modeling procedure
constraints: The article states it is a relational study, so cause-effect relationships cannot be extrapolated
The relationship between negative emotions and resilience through the SEM was not significant
target_learners: secondary school students aged 14–19 in Physical Education classes
target_learning_goals: adoption of healthy physical activity habits
examples: The hypothesized model was tested with maximum likelihood estimation and bootstrapping on data from 615 students and was accepted as suitable
